verification_report.summary:
The complete submitted chapter passes the sequential audit relative to the accepted inputs. This verdict is CONDITIONAL on the exact global analytic approximants and restricted divisorial bounds from analytic_approximation_01: its verification report was still absent at the final dependency check. Their uses here have the required hypotheses; their independent verification is not claimed.

The image ideals are coherent and nonzero by generic zero Lelong number and Skoda integrability. Superadditivity with nonnegative remainders proves the full real-parameter Fekete limit, its supremum formula, and equality with the integer limit. Exact restricted analytic type and the accepted Gauduchon bound make that limit finite on each fixed compact modification. Multiplier-ideal invariance, homogeneity, and the stated sum/maximum inequalities have the correct directions. The genuine-restriction comparison follows from local Bergman lower bounds; the log-resolution estimate with fixed discrepancy loss proves analytic equality. The strict local example is valid.

On a curve, finite-subset limits of the approximant mass bounds prove that D_u is countably supported and finite, with 0<=d<=M. The uniform Green-kernel L1 bound justifies the infinite integral and distributional equation ddc w=D_u-d eta; it introduces no diffuse residual current. Poisson correction gives the claimed positive current and extended measure. Changing the volume form or admissible smooth background changes the constructed representative smoothly, so its ordinary type is canonical. Equality of curve Lelong numbers determines multiplier ideals, but is correctly distinguished from ordinary equivalence.

Coefficient domination by D_u proves total-variation convergence of D_m. Superadditivity gives dyadic increase of the measures, hence decrease of their nonpositive Green potentials; monotone convergence identifies the pointwise limit even at poles, and the kernel bound proves L1 convergence. Finite logarithmic parts establish the ordinary types of restricted approximants and analytic restrictions. For a genuine arbitrary restriction, positivity of the residual distribution gives the stated ordinary singularity inequality.

The complete equation theorem passes. The zero-integral Poisson equation and p>1 yield a bounded continuous correction. For any competitor in the prescribed ordinary type, subtracting w gives a bounded qpsh representative; bounded Bedford-Taylor noncharging then excludes diffuse polar residual mass. Thus its extended measure is exactly its full current minus D_u and has mass M-d. This forces c=(M-d)/integral_Y f dV, proves existence precisely when M>d for c>0, and reduces uniqueness to harmonic constancy. The M=d endpoint, including M=d=0, is also valid.

The cited statements and normalization were checked against the supplied Demailly and SGPT sources, using theorem search first and web fallback where needed. No BMP/PVP, globalization of arbitrary local modifications, higher-dimensional realization, addition equality, or identification with the full SGPT P-trace is used. Fifteen statement checks and eight reference/dependency checks are persisted. No mathematical errors or gaps were found.
